description: You woke in bottomland where the creek braids through. Water is close and the growth is thick — food grows here, but the ground is soft and the creek rises fast when it rains.
hazard: Flash floods in heavy rain. The creek can take a tile for a day.
name: Creek Bottom
tagline: Water close, growth thick, ground soft

description: You woke on high ground with the wind in your face. You can see for miles — but there's little cover, little water, and the nights bite.
hazard: Exposed. Cold wind at night costs extra calories to stay warm.
name: Ridgeline

description: You woke among the bones of a suburb — cracked streets, empty houses, a stripped grocery. Scavenging is rich here. Foraging is not.
hazard: Thin wild food. The houses feed you until they don't.
name: Old Suburb
tagline: Ruins close, pickings rich, woods thin

description: You woke in pine flatland — straight trunks, needle floor, deep shade. Game trails cross everywhere. Plant food is sparse but the hunting is honest.
hazard: Dark under the canopy. Easy to get turned around.
name: Pine Flat
tagline: Deep woods, game sign, thin greens

description: You woke on low ground the river reclaims every spring. The soil is black and everything grows — when the water lets it.
hazard: Standing water breeds mosquitoes and bad luck in equal measure.
name: Floodplain
tagline: Black soil, high water, fast growth

description: You woke in the rows of a dead orchard — apple, pear, persimmon, gone feral. Fruit hangs where the rows still hold. Between the rows: meadow.
hazard: The orchard feeds everything — including things with teeth.
name: Orchard Rows

description: You woke at the edge of a worked-out quarry — stone walls, scrub, a deep still pit of water. Little grows. Much can be built.
hazard: Stone and scrub. You'll work for every calorie that isn't scavenged.
name: Quarry Edge

description: You woke where the river bends under a limestone bluff — creek below, hardwoods above, a cave mouth in the rock face. A little of everything.
hazard: The cave is shelter and a question mark.
name: River Bluff

description: You woke where a wildfire ran through years back. The snags stand white and the ash is deep — sightlines go forever, cover goes nowhere, and the new growth is coming in thick and hungry.
hazard: Dead snags fall without warning in wind. Ash gets in everything, including lungs.
name: Burn Scar
tagline: Open ash, dead snags, new green

description: You woke on a hummock in the swamp — dry feet, for now. Black water braids between the rises, frogs never stop, and everything edible here has to be reached by wading.
hazard: Footing is treacherous and the water hides depth. Mosquitoes own the dusk.
name: Swamp Hummock
tagline: Black water, high ground in patches

description: You woke in a mill town — brick shells, a rusted water tower, houses gone to weather. The easy scavenging is long gone, but the bones of industry are everywhere: tools, wire, things built to last.
hazard: Rusted metal everywhere. Tetanus country — mind every cut.
name: Mill Town

description: You woke in an abandoned campground — fire rings gone cold, tent pads, a bear box hanging open. Other people were here. Recently, by the look of the ashes. Whether that is good news depends on the people.
hazard: Other people were here recently. They may come back.
name: Old Campground

description: You woke where a river slough goes black and still under bald cypress — knees rising like knuckles, fallen timber just under the surface. Fish, frogs, and turtles are thick here. The water hides what it hides.
hazard: Cottonmouths den in the fallen timber, and the snags under black water will roll a wading leg.
name: Cypress Slough
tagline: Black water, cypress knees, hidden timber

description: You woke above a beaver pond — a dam of gnawed sticks holding back a whole small lake. The engineers are still at it: fresh cuttings every morning, wood that arrives already felled. Fish, frogs, ducks, and water you can mostly trust.
hazard: Dams fail in storms. A pond can become a flood in an hour, and the engineers do not warn you first.
name: Beaver Pond

description: You woke in a pecan grove gone wild — rows of old trees dropping more nuts than anything can eat. In a mast year this place is a calorie vault: pounds of fat and protein falling out of the sky. Everything with teeth in the county knows it.
hazard: Mast is seasonal. In spring this grove is a rumor — and the boar remember exactly where it is.
name: Pecan Grove

description: You woke at the edge of a hay field — acres of grass going to seed, no cover, nowhere to hide. Rabbits and deer work the edges at dawn and dusk. Everything sees you coming, including you.
hazard: No cover and no shade. Storms see you coming from miles off — and so does anything watching.
name: Hay Field
tagline: Open ground, honest sign, no cover

description: You woke at the edge of a junkyard — cars stacked like cordwood, appliances rusting in rows, a mountain of tires gone to moss. Nothing edible grows here. But the bones of the old world are thick: wire, sheet metal, tools that only need cleaning.
hazard: Tetanus country. Stacks shift without warning, and something dens in the tire mountain.
name: Junkyard Edge

description: You woke beside the grain silo at the old co-op — a concrete tower that once held a harvest. Grain is still in there, maybe, behind the rusted auger housing. So are the rats, the mold, and ten years of dust.
hazard: Spoiled grain kills as surely as hunger. The dust hangs in the air and the tower sheds concrete.
name: Grain Silo

description: You woke under a fire lookout tower on a bare knob — a steel skeleton with a cabin on top and the whole country laid out below it. From the cab you can see weather coming a day away. So can everything else.
hazard: Lightning loves this hill. The cabin is shelter; the steel is a promise.
name: Lookout Tower

description: You woke in a cedar thicket — evergreen dark, needle floor, the air sharp with resin. Deer yard here in hard weather, shoulder to shoulder under the boughs. The cover is total and the walking is terrible.
hazard: Ticks by the hundred. The canopy eats the sky; it is easy to walk in circles all day.
name: Cedar Thicket
